newsitem.title: UK: Peel shares build on upbeat results.
newsitem.headline: Peel shares build on upbeat results.

text.p: Shares in property group Peel Holdings Plc rose on Thursday after the company posted a rise in profits and asset values coupled with an upbeat statement on prospects.
The stock was quoted up 21-1/2p, or 3.9 percent, at 540 by 0923 GMT.
Peel said pre-tax profit rose 8.9 percent to 13.7 million stg in the year ended March 31 from 12.6 million a year before and raised its dividend to 8.0p from 6.5p.

It said its UK investment portfolio excluding the Trafford Centre -- its flagship retail development in Manchester, northern England -- had been valued at 427.7 million stg, producing an underlying valuation surplus of 31.1 million stg.
The valuation of the Trafford Centre had been raised by 97 million stg to 200 million and more than 65 percent of space had been let, with construction on target for completion in Autumn 1998.

"The group is optimistic about prospects for its various operations in the coming year and encouraged by the expectation that rental growth amongst its commercial properties is spreading," said chairman John Whittaker.
He said the group was pursuing a strategy that "will deliver superior total returns to shareholders on a sustainable basis."
